title: Cayley access models for matrix functions: reachable class and cost
summary: We study how to compute $f(A)b$ on a quantum computer, where $A$ is Hermitian. When $f$ is nonsmooth or has localized difficulty in the spectrum, classical numerical linear algebra approximates it with rational functions rather than polynomials. We propose the Cayley transform, parameterized by $σ\in \mathbb{R}$ and $γ> 0$, as an alternative to the standard quantum access model. The two parameters let one concentrate accuracy where $f$ is difficult, which standard models can achieve only by raising the polynomial degree globally.
